{{short description|Australian–American mathematician}}
{{For|the Canadian writer|James Macdonald Oxley}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=April 2022}}
'''James G. Oxley''' is an Australian–American [[mathematician]], Boyd Professor of Mathematics at [[Louisiana State University]].<ref>[http://www.lsu.edu/ur/ocur/lsunews/MediaCenter/News/2012/12/item55843.html LSU Mathematician Named Boyd Professor] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130404003652/http://www.lsu.edu/ur/ocur/lsunews/MediaCenter/News/2012/12/item55843.html |date=2013-04-04 }}, Louisiana State University, December 7, 2012, retrieved 2013-03-20.</ref> He is known for his expertise in [[matroid theory]] and [[graph theory]].

Oxley did his undergraduate studies in Australia,<ref name="cv">[https://www.math.lsu.edu/~oxley/briefvita.pdf Brief vita], retrieved 2013-03-20.</ref> and earned a doctorate from the [[University of Oxford]] in 1978, under the supervision of [[Dominic Welsh]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=11323|name=James G. Oxley}}.</ref> He joined the Louisiana State University faculty in 1982.<ref name="cv"/>

Oxley is the author of the book ''Matroid Theory'' (Oxford University Press, 1992).

In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-03-20.</ref>
